title: Every reactor mutation is a job moving through five statuses, of which only READ_READY and FAILED are terminal
content:
Every mutation in the reactor is processed as a **job**, and the job — not the action — is the unit whose progress you can observe. Jobs move through:

```
PENDING -> RUNNING -> WRITE_READY -> READ_READY
                   \-> FAILED
```

- `PENDING` — queued, not yet started.
- `RUNNING` — the reducer is executing.
- `WRITE_READY` — operations have been written to the operation store.
- `READ_READY` — all read models have finished processing; the document is fully readable.
- `FAILED` — an unrecoverable error.

Only `READ_READY` and `FAILED` are terminal. `WRITE_READY` is the subtle one: the operation is durably persisted at that point, but the read models have not caught up, so a read issued immediately may not see the change. That gap is exactly what the extra hop to `READ_READY` closes.

This is why the two client entry points behave so differently. `IReactorClient.execute()` waits until the job reaches `READ_READY` before resolving — you get read-after-write consistency, at the cost of blocking through the read-model phase. `executeAsync()` returns immediately with a `JobInfo` still at `PENDING`; you then either poll `getJobStatus(jobId)` or await `waitForJob(job.id)`.

```typescript
const job = await reactorClient.executeAsync(docId, "main", actions);
const completed = await reactorClient.waitForJob(job.id);
```

The distinction matters for anything that writes on a hot path. Processors, for instance, must use their `dispatch` handle (which wraps `executeAsync`) rather than a blocking `execute()`, because a processor that waits for `READ_READY` can block on the very pipeline it is part of.

The status enum is mirrored by the event bus: `JOB_PENDING` (10001), `JOB_RUNNING` (10002), `JOB_WRITE_READY` (10003), `JOB_READ_READY` (10004), `JOB_FAILED` (10005).

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/01-Reactor/01-WorkingWithTheReactor.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: PENDING to RUNNING to WRITE_READY to READ_READY, or FAILED. execute() waits for READ_READY; executeAsync() returns at PENDING.
